mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within three months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased wage pressures and higher corporate costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.5% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth, positively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where real estate sales increased by more than 5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals a contraction in supply, leading to increased prices and reduced corporate profitability, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where industrial production decreased by more than 2% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable monetary policy, which supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over two consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, positively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000 over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% each over the last quarter signals a broad-based economic expansion, positively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where both real GDP and retail sales increased by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.5%, it indicates a tight monetary policy in a tight labor market, leading to increased borrowing costs and wage pressures, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and UNRATE was below 4.5%.
